kept.q: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of obtaining a number greater than 4?
kept.explanation: The numbers greater than 4 on a die are 5 and 6, giving 2 favourable outcomes out of 6. So the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.
kept.pidgin: Na 5 and 6 be di numbers wey dey greater than 4 for die, e give us 2 out of 6. When you reduce am, e come be 2/6 = 1/3.

kept.q: Musa has two bags. Bag A contains 3 red beads and 2 black beads. Bag B contains 4 red beads and 1 black bead. If he picks one bead at random from each bag, what is the probability that both beads are red?
kept.explanation: The probability of red from Bag A is 3/5 and from Bag B is 4/5. Since the picks are independent, multiply: (3/5) x (4/5) = 12/25.
kept.pidgin: Probability say red go come out for Bag A na 3/5, and for Bag B na 4/5. Since dem dey independent, just multiply dem: (3/5) x (4/5) = 12/25.

kept.q: A box contains 5 good phone chargers and 3 faulty ones, all looking alike. Two chargers are picked one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both chargers picked are faulty?
kept.explanation: The probability the first is faulty is 3/8. Without replacement, the probability the second is also faulty is 2/7. Multiplying gives (3/8) x (2/7) = 6/56 = 3/28.
kept.pidgin: Probability for first faulty charger na 3/8, and since dem no return am, di second one na 2/7. Multiply dem together to get (3/8) x (2/7) = 3/28.

kept.q: In a class of 40 students, 18 study Physics, 15 study Chemistry, and 7 study both Physics and Chemistry. If a student is picked at random from the class, what is the probability that the student studies Physics or Chemistry?
kept.explanation: Using the addition rule, P(Physics or Chemistry) = P(Physics) + P(Chemistry) - P(both) = 18/40 + 15/40 - 7/40 = 26/40. This accounts for students counted twice in both subjects.
kept.pidgin: We go use addition rule, add Physics and Chemistry, then minus di ones wey do both. E go give us 18/40 + 15/40 - 7/40 = 26/40.

kept.q: A fair coin is tossed and a fair die is rolled together. What is the probability of getting a tail on the coin and an even number on the die?
kept.explanation: The probability of a tail is 1/2 and the probability of an even number (2, 4, or 6) is 3/6 = 1/2. Since the events are independent, multiply: (1/2) x (1/2) = 1/4.
kept.pidgin: Probability for tail na 1/2, while even number for die na 3/6 which be 1/2. Multiply di two independent probabilities to get (1/2) x (1/2) = 1/4.

kept.q: A hawker at Onitsha market has 20 oranges, of which 4 are bad. If 3 oranges are selected at random without replacement, what is the probability that all 3 selected oranges are good?
kept.explanation: There are 16 good oranges out of 20. The probability all three picked are good is (16/20) x (15/19) x (14/18) = 3360/6840 = 560/1140, when simplified using successive conditional probabilities without replacement.
kept.pidgin: We get 16 good oranges out of 20, and we dey pick dem one after di other without replacement. As we multiply di probabilities, e go give us 560/1140.

kept.q: Two events P and Q are such that P(P) = 0.3, P(Q) = 0.25, and P(P and Q) = 0.1. Find P(P or Q).
kept.explanation: Using the addition rule for probability, P(P or Q) = P(P) + P(Q) - P(P and Q) = 0.3 + 0.25 - 0.1 = 0.45. This avoids double counting the overlap.
kept.pidgin: To find P(P or Q), we go add P(P) and P(Q) then minus di intersection. E go give us 0.3 + 0.25 - 0.1 = 0.45.

kept.q: A bag contains 8 balls numbered 1 to 8. A ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that the number on the ball is a multiple of 3 or a multiple of 4?
kept.explanation: Multiples of 3 up to 8 are 3 and 6 (2 numbers), while multiples of 4 are 4 and 8 (2 numbers), with no overlap. So the total favourable outcomes are 4 out of 8, giving 4/8 = 1/2.
kept.pidgin: Multiples of 3 na 3 and 6, while multiples of 4 na 4 and 8, wey make dem 4 favourable numbers in total. So di probability na 4/8 = 1/2.
